title: Retained RVC disposable Gateway technical smoke
question: Can the current retained one-profile RVC technical profile complete the frozen Gateway v1 lifecycle on a disposable loopback Gateway without accepting malformed or stale PCM?
hypothesis: The exact retained RVC technical profile, identified by its profile, configuration, and pipeline hashes, can authenticate and attach through the Gateway, transform one synthetic 28-frame generation at 20 ms pacing (a 25-frame RVC batch plus a three-frame tail before end) into finite normalized changed PCM with preserved frame identity, reject generation-2 stale output after cancel, and close its disposable session cleanly.

control.description: A deterministic in-memory Gateway contract fake that batches 25 frames, flushes a short final tail, and injects one post-cancel stale frame for local-gate verification.

variants.description: One explicitly enabled current retained RVC technical-validation profile through an externally launched or auto-launched loopback-only Gateway.

fixtures.manifest: In-memory deterministic non-speech float32 PCM generator

environment.git_commit: A persisted trace requires the exact clean checked-out Git commit.
environment.runtime: Python 3.12 workspace lock, frozen protocol v1, and the current retained ignored RVC profile/runtime inputs.
environment.hardware: Record only separately retained operator metadata outside Git; the tracked runner persists no host, artifact-path, credential, or raw-audio fields.

model_revisions.rvc: Bind through the Gateway's profile, configuration, and pipeline identities; the trace contains only public hashes and no artifact locations.

procedure.summary: Run deterministic fake checks first. In an explicitly opted-in live run, load exactly one ignored technical RVC worker profile through ProfileRegistry, bind its public profile and configuration hashes to an exactly-one-entry Gateway catalog before session creation, create an authenticated session, attach with the exact Extension Origin and one-use ticket, require the exact 1000 ms/50-frame Gateway advertisement, run one normal generation of 28 frames at 20 ms pacing (25-frame inference batch plus a three-frame tail) and end it, cancel generation 2 under a local stale-output gate, then acknowledge session.close and confirm that both a following DELETE and GET return 404 because the close already invalidated the session. Auto-launch pins its base ingress budget to 500 ms; the retained profile's 500 ms minimum context produces the required 1000 ms session budget. Ordinary network and post-start control waits remain short and bounded. Auto-launch readiness and generation.ready use a separate bounded cold-start timeout: the larger of 180 seconds and the selected profile's first_output_ms envelope; it does not change 20 ms pacing. This trace proves only the Gateway-visible 50-frame ingress credit, client high-water bound, and 28-frame drain without overflow or fallback. The separate delayed-worker service regression proves WorkerBridge's private 25-frame accepted cap; both evidence records are required.
procedure.warmup: Gateway readiness and any worker warmup are operational prerequisites only and are excluded from all latency claims.
invalidation_conditions: The persisted trace is not bound to the exact clean checked-out Git commit.

The live route uses more than one profile, a profile whose catalog/session/attach identities do not bind the current retained RVC technical profile, a Gateway URL whose HTTP or HTTPS host is not loopback, or more than one allowed session.

The retained profile document or catalog has anything other than exactly one matching technical RVC worker profile; catalog, session, attach, or generation identities disagree; session protocol_version is not 1; authentication or exact-Origin attachment fails; the Gateway advertisement is not exactly 1000 ms and 50 frames or the client high-water exceeds it; the 28-frame generation overflows or falls back instead of draining; the separate delayed-worker service regression does not prove the private 25-frame accepted cap; or a generation accepts malformed, non-finite, out-of-range, reordered, timestamp-mismatched, unchanged, or stale output.
The trace contains a credential, ticket, voice identifier, artifact/runtime path, worker endpoint, raw PCM, payload digest, free-form server error, or raw sample data.
A technical result is represented as quality, speaker, content, latency, authorization, licensing, security, deployment, or production-readiness evidence.

decision_rule: The experiment decision is always inconclusive. A technical pass requires one current retained RVC technical worker profile loaded from the ignored configuration through ProfileRegistry, an exactly-one-entry catalog whose profile and configuration hashes match that configuration before session creation, matching catalog/session/attach/generation profile, configuration, and pipeline identities, session protocol_version 1, authenticated exact-Origin attachment, an exact Gateway advertisement of 1000 ms and 50 ingress frames with client high-water at or below 50, one normal 28-frame generation-1 run at 20 ms pacing (25-frame full batch plus a three-frame tail before end) that drains without overflow or fallback and has contiguous sequence and echoed timestamps, finite normalized changed output, a locally gated generation-2 cancellation with zero accepted stale frames, and acknowledged session.close followed by DELETE 404 and GET 404. The delayed-worker service regression must separately prove WorkerBridge's private 25-frame accepted cap; EXP-004 does not observe that private cap. It does not establish voice conversion quality, target speaker change, Japanese content preservation, latency, authorization, license status, security, deployment, or production readiness.

artifact_policy.raw_location: Synthetic PCM remains only in process memory. Optional metadata-only traces are written to an operator-selected location outside the repository.
artifact_policy.git_contents: Plan, runner source, deterministic fake tests, trace schema, and no real-run trace, artifacts, credentials, reference voices, weights, paths, or PCM.
artifact_policy.retention: Delete optional local trace output after review or within 14 days. The runner does not persist PCM.
artifact_policy.authorization: Only project-authored synthetic non-speech PCM is sent by this experiment. The separately authorized retained RVC target and runtime remain outside Git and are never named in the trace.
